topic.coverageNote: Open clinical review of DISH. It gives the non-inflammatory entheseal definition, the anterior-longitudinal-ligament mechanism, the Resnick criteria for the thoracic spine, the contrast with ankylosing spondylitis, and the associated metabolic conditions.

mcqs.question: How does this review define diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis?

options.A: A systemic non-inflammatory disease characterised by ossification of the entheses
options.D: A disease limited to the hands

mcqs.explanation: The review defines DISH as a systemic non-inflammatory disease characterised by ossification of the entheses.

sourceRefs.excerpt: DISH) is a systemic noninflammatory disease characterized by ossification of the entheses.

mcqs.question: Which structure do current theories in this review put at the centre of the spinal disease?
mcqs.explanation: The review says current theories focus on pathologic calcification of the anterior longitudinal ligament as the main mechanism.

sourceRefs.excerpt: pathologic calcification of the anterior longitudinal ligament of the spine as the main physiopathological mechanism of disease.

mcqs.question: Which spinal findings does the review quote as the Resnick criteria?

options.A: Anterolateral ossification of at least four contiguous thoracic segments, preserved disc spaces, and no apophyseal degeneration or sacroiliac inflammatory changes
options.B: Ossification of one lumbar segment with sacroiliac erosions
options.C: Bilateral sacroiliitis and slender vertical syndesmophytes

mcqs.explanation: The review states anterolateral ossification of at least four contiguous thoracic vertebral segments, preservation of the intervertebral disc spaces, and absence of apophyseal joint degeneration or sacroiliac inflammatory changes.

sourceRefs.excerpt: anterolateral ossifications of at least four contiguous thoracic vertebral segments, preservation of the intervertebral disk spaces, and absence of apophyseal joint degeneration or sacroiliac inflammatory changes [ ].[ ]

mcqs.question: How does the review contrast the bony bridges of ankylosing spondylitis with DISH?

options.A: They are slender and vertical, involve the outer annulus, and do not involve the anterior longitudinal ligament
options.B: They are identical to DISH bridges
options.C: They always spare the annulus and involve only the anterior longitudinal ligament
options.D: The review says ankylosing spondylitis cannot be distinguished

mcqs.explanation: The review says ankylosing-spondylitis bridges are slender and vertical, involve the outer margin of the annulus, and do not involve the anterior longitudinal ligament. Sacroiliac and apophyseal erosions and ankylosis are not seen in DISH.

sourceRefs.excerpt: in Ankylosing Spondylitis, the bony bridges are slender, vertical, and involve the outer margin of the annulus fibrosus and do not involve the anterior longitudinal ligament.

mcqs.question: Which comorbidities does the review list with DISH?

options.A: Obesity, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hyperinsulinaemia, dyslipidaemia, and hyperuricaemia

mcqs.explanation: The review says comorbidities include obesity, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hyperinsulinaemia, dyslipidaemia, and hyperuricaemia.
